title: Memory versus context selection: can memory change degradation at smaller selection budgets?
question: Does lexical memory change observed degradation with smaller block-selection budgets?
hypothesis: Memory may recover alias recall without recovering information lost through attention selection or compression.
failure_interpretation: Context-sensitive behavior may fail despite changed memory or selection settings.
controls: Fix tokenizer, dataset source and packing within each selected data route.
Fix seed-matched model width, depth, heads, optimizer, runtime, budget, evaluator, and endpoint policy unless a listed axis changes.
Report held-out language-model loss separately from each capability card category.
confounders: Model-construction RNG changes when module inventories differ.
Approximate scale classes rather than matched parameter counts.
Educational-kernel overhead is not an architecture-speed measurement.
hardware_notes: Tiny is the recommended class; Python timing is not an architectural verdict.
runtime_class: Qualitative scale-dependent educational PyTorch workload; measure local runtime rather than inferring timing.

papers.title: Engram

can_establish: Controlled endpoint deltas for the declared attention and memory contrasts.
cannot_establish: An interaction statistic, synergy claim, speed claim, or a claim that current MLA cache matches paper-equivalent compression.
prerequisites: Block-sparse selection is a local educational design; batch/head unions can exceed a per-head selection budget.
